Subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Hi Samir,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time and for walking us through Acme's roadmap and AI use cases. Quick recap and a few asks so we can build a target benchmark for pricing and next steps: 

Summary from the call:
- Primary use: customer support auto-summaries + intent routing, peak QPS during launches.
- Expected steady-state traffic: 50M tokens/month initially, growing to ~250M tokens/month in 9-12 months.
- Latency target: 150-250ms p95 on short-chat flows (<=512 tokens).

Asks for the pricing benchmark spreadsheet:
1) Confirm approximate token volumes (you mentioned 40-60M/month to start — is 50M a good working number?).
2) Budget range for inference (monthly or target $/1M tokens). If you have a target $/1M tokens we should try to hit, please share.
3) Any procurement timing constraints or required contract terms (SaaS vs Dedicated, SOC2 evidence, etc.).

What I'll send next: an initial target-price benchmarking sheet comparing Redwood unit economics vs OpenAI and Anthropic for your workload (taking into account batching, KV cache benefits, and quantized open-model hosting economics). Attached: redwood-pricing-compare.xlsx (initial figures) and a placeholder token forecast you can edit.

Proposed next step: If the target numbers look reasonable, we can schedule a 30-min pricing/tech deep-dive with Marissa (cost modeling) and our solutions engineer next week to align on a pilot.

Thanks — looking forward to your numbers.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Vanessa — thanks for the quick recap and the file. Confirming the traffic numbers: yes, 50M tokens/month initial is accurate; 200-300M/month is our internal ramp target within 9-12 months (we're modeling 250M as the conservative ramp).

On budget: our procurement team is targeting a unit economics target in the $150-200 per 1M tokens range for inference (including any host + model costs). For context, we've been quoted roughly $300+/1M from managed OpenAI offers for comparable throughput, and Anthropic came back in the ~$220-260 range depending on reserved capacity.

We have a procurement window in late July for the pilot vendor selection. Our key questions for your benchmarking sheet:
- Does the Redwood figure include network and storage egress costs if we choose hosted vs dedicated?
- How much upside on unit economics do we expect from batching and KV caching for our mix (short chat + summarization)?

CC'd Acme Billing (billing@acme.com) for budget visibility.

On availability — I'm free for the pricing/tech deep-dive next Tue/Wed morning PT.

> 
> On budget: our procurement team is targeting a unit economics target in the $150-200 per 1M tokens range for inference (including any host + model costs). For context, we've been quoted roughly $300+/1M from managed OpenAI offers for comparable throughput, and Anthropic came back in the ~$220-260 range depending on reserved capacity.

Thanks — that helps a lot. Quick answers and initial benchmarking takeaways (high level):

1) What the attached sheet includes:
- Fully loaded $/1M tokens for hosted Redwood (model + compute + network amortized across forecasted tokens)
- Reserved/Dedicated capacity scenarios (committed throughput discounts)
- Open-model host variant: estimated $/1M when using quantized open models (costs assume 8-bit quantization, lower GPU slots per host)
- Simple comparison rows for OpenAI and Anthropic public/quoted rates for the model class you described.

2) About egress/network/storage: Hosted Redwood estimates include typical cloud network egress within the same region but exclude third-party cross-region egress costs — we flag those in the notes. Dedicated/Private quotes can be modeled to include your networking profile if needed.

3) Batching & KV cache upside: For your mixed-workload (short-chat + summarization) we model ~20-35% token-cost reduction from effective batching and ~10-20% additional reduction from KV/prefix caching on repeated context — aggregated upside ~25-40% depending on sequence length distribution. Those are reflected in the "optimized" rows in the sheet.

Initial target benchmarking vs your targets:
- OpenAI (managed): quoted ~300+/1M for comparable SLA — typical for their managed stacks on high throughput.
- Anthropic (managed): ~220-260/1M depending on reserved commitment.
- Redwood hosted (optimized for your forecast): baseline ~210/1M, optimized (batching + KV + reserved) ~135-175/1M.
- Redwood dedicated (reserved GPUs + quantized open model): can go lower toward ~100-140/1M at scale and with a 12-month commit (depends on model choice and QPS profile).

Given your procurement target of $150-200/1M, the Redwood optimized hosted scenario sits squarely in that range for your initial volumes; dedicated/reserved options present further upside as you scale.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached sheet and the live Google sheet (link below) — edit the token forecast tabs where you see fit.
- If the headline numbers look aligned, let's lock a 30-min slot Tue 6/15 9:30am PT for a pricing deep-dive with Marissa and our infra engineer to produce a formal pilot quote and optional reserved pricing.
